# Black History Month

> > Official U.S. government portal for Black History Month featuring resources from the Library of Congress, Smithsonian Institution, National Archives, and National Museum of African American History and Culture.

This site serves as the federal government's central hub for Black History Month observances, educational materials, and cultural programming. It aggregates content from major institutions including the National Gallery of Art, National Park Service, and National Endowment for the Humanities, highlighting figures like Carter G. Woodson, Frederick Douglass, and W. E. B. Du Bois.

## Key Topics

- Library of Congress
- National Museum of African American History and Culture
- Smithsonian Institution
- National Archives and Records Administration
- Carter G. Woodson
- Frederick Douglass
- W. E. B. Du Bois
- Association for the Study of Negro Life and History (ASNLH)
- Civil Rights Movement
- Negro History Week
- African American History
- National Gallery of Art
- National Park Service
- National Endowment for the Humanities
- Federal cultural resources

## About & Overview

- [About Black History Month](https://www.blackhistorymonth.gov/About.html): About Black History Month & federal partners like Library of Congress

## Events & Programming

- [2026 Events Calendar](https://www.blackhistorymonth.gov/Events.html): 2026 events calendar featuring Smithsonian Jazz & Library of Congress

## Educational Resources

- [Resources for Teachers](https://www.blackhistorymonth.gov/ForTeachers.html): Teacher resources & lesson plans on Jacob Lawrence, Frederick Douglass

## Exhibits & Collections

- [Museum Exhibits and Collections](https://www.blackhistorymonth.gov/ExhibitsandCollections.html): Museum exhibits featuring Sam Gilliam & African American History Museum

## Archives & Media

- [Historical Images](https://www.blackhistorymonth.gov/Images.html): Historical images & photos from Civil Rights March, John Lewis archives
- [Audio and Video Archives](https://www.blackhistorymonth.gov/AudioandVideo.html): Audio/video archives from Library of Congress & public broadcasting
